transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM), Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Maya Lopez (Northstar Head of ML), Ben Carter (Northstar Platform), Nadia Wu (Northstar Finance), Omar Rahman (Northstar SRE)

[00:00] Samira Khan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — usage review, cost drivers, reliability post-black friday, and roadmap alignment for Q1. if we miss anything shout it out.
[00:18] Maya Lopez: thanks samira, yeah real quick — congrats on the new quantization docs we saw last week. want to start with the usage because we had a surprising spike in november, uh, right around black friday.
[00:30] Ben Carter: yeah to add, the spike wasn't just queries, it was a bunch of small model churns from our personalization service, so we saw a lot of short-lived sessions that bloomed the token count.
[00:44] Priya Desai: mmhm, that's consistent with what we saw in the telemetry — prefix cache miss rate jumped which increased per-request compute. did you have the burst windows broken down?
[00:55] Ben Carter: i've got a rough CSV. i can share the 3-hour windows where qps doubled. i'll add to the drive after.
[01:06] Ethan Cole: perfect — for context for finance, can you summarize the cost impact, nadia?
[01:12] Nadia Wu: sure — the spike added about 22% to december projected spend, mostly from pay-as-you-go hosting; reserved instance utilization was lower than expected because the bursting shifted load to non-reserved queues.
[01:26] Samira Khan: thanks. so couple levers — smarter routing to Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, prefix/KV cache tuning, and batch sizing. priya, can you give quick notes on options we recommended?
[01:40] Priya Desai: yeah, high level: 1) tune prefix cache to reduce misses for personalization prefixes (should cut token generation by ~15%), 2) use session-affinity routing so short-lived sessions land on cheaper pools with smaller kv overhead, 3) consider a modest reserved capacity increment for peak windows and burst credits. also quantized model variant we tested reduces per-token GPU time by ~18% on similar prompts but there are edge cases for hallucination — need eval suites.
[02:10] Maya Lopez: the hallucination risk is the key for product. we can't afford quality regressions for customer-facing recs. how confident are we?
[02:18] Priya Desai: medium confidence — we saw paraphrase quality hold for the sampled evals, but the personalization prompts have some long context dependencies, so we'll run a targeted eval set.
[02:30] Omar Rahman: on reliability — we had that 11/27 incident where autoscaler delayed adding nodes for 7 minutes. we traced it to a race in the node drain logic and slow healthchecks during the spike. remediation?
[02:46] Priya Desai: we pushed a config change to decrease healthcheck thresholds and added a faster warmup path for KV cache; those changes are in canary. we also recommended redundant pools so a failing scaling op doesn't take down all capacity.
[03:02] Ben Carter: ok that sounds good. question from finance: if we move to dedicated and reserve more, what's the break-even on spend vs current hybrid model? can you run a blended model calc?
[03:14] Samira Khan: yes — we'll model three scenarios: current hybrid with burst credits, 20% reserved capacity bump, and 40% reserved bump with autoscaling credits. we'll put the unit economics (per-token cost, latency percentiles) side-by-side.
[03:28] Nadia Wu: timeline: finance needs numbers by 12/24 to decide for january commit. is that feasible?
[03:34] Ethan Cole: feasible if ben gives the detailed 90-day usage by 12/22.
[03:38] Ben Carter: i'll get that.
[03:40] Priya Desai: also, for compliance — you brought up KMS and audit logs previously. we have a short doc on KMS integration with Redwood Private and with our hosted offering's customer-managed keys. link will be in the follow-up. the Private deployment package supports HSM integration too but that's longer lead time.
[03:58] Maya Lopez: security is non-negotiable. we need SOC2 plus proof of key separation in the canary. can you provide redwood audit log retention options?
[04:08] Ethan Cole: yep — we have standard 90-day logs, an extended 1-year option as an add-on, and enterprise retention with S3 export. we'll attach the SOC2 summary and log retention matrix.
[04:20] Maya Lopez: thanks.
[04:22] [brief crosstalk]
[04:30] Samira Khan: switching to roadmap — northstar's priorities for Q1 are personalization scale and lower latency on mobile recs. we proposed a staged Dedicated rollout: 1) pilot on non-critical traffic in late jan, 2) expand to 40% of recs by march with traffic-splitting and A/B for quality, 3) full cutover only if quality holds.
[04:56] Ben Carter: for the pilot, we need canary runbooks and rollback steps. priya, do you have a sample?
[05:04] Priya Desai: yes, we have a documented canary checklist — includes traffic thresholds, latency SLOs, and automated rollback triggers. we'll share that. also recommend a pre-run micro-benchmark using your most common prompt shapes.
[05:18] Omar Rahman: about observability — can we get per-model token-level traces and cold-start heatmaps? we had blind spots during the spike.
[05:27] Priya Desai: we can provide token-level breakdowns and a heatmap export. there is a small retention cost but it's usually worth it for debugging.
[05:36] Nadia Wu: quick procurement question — if we sign a reserved commitment now, how flexible are the term adjustments if actual usage is off?
[05:45] Samira Khan: we have rollover credits and a one-time mid-term adjustment clause for the first year; we'll detail that in the commercial note.
[05:53] Maya Lopez: ok, let's capture open risks: 1) quality regression from quantized models, 2) autoscaler delays during very sharp spikes, 3) budgeting mismatch if spikes recur.
[06:05] Ethan Cole: agreed — to mitigate: run targeted evals, canary faster healthchecks, and present blended economics for finance.
[06:12] Ben Carter: i also want to test session-affinity routing in a sandbox. can redwood enable that on our staging?
[06:20] Priya Desai: yes — we can enable session-affinity routing for staging; we'll need a staging key and a short config window.
[06:29] Samira Khan: ok great. recap and owners:
- [06:34] Ben Carter: provide 90-day usage & peak traces (due 2026-12-22)
- [06:38] Nadia Wu: confirm budget envelope (due 2026-12-24)
- [06:42] Samira Khan: send pricing scenarios + slot utilization spreadsheet (due 2026-12-23)
- [06:46] Priya Desai: run quantized micro-benchmark + targeted evals (due 2026-12-27)
- [06:50] Ethan Cole: share SOC2 summary, log retention options, and KMS integration note (due 2026-12-22)

[06:52] Maya Lopez: that all looks good. last thing — can we get a short one-pager on recommended staging run plan so our platform team can schedule work?
[06:59] Samira Khan: yes, we'll produce a one-pager and attach the canary checklist.

[07:05] Omar Rahman: thanks everyone. appreciate the practical steps.
[07:08] Samira Khan: thanks all — we'll follow up in email and get the workshop on the calendar for early jan.
[07:14] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few proper-noun swaps (e.g., KV "cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in parts) and occasional punctuation issues. links shared during call: [pricing-spreadsheet-link], [kms-integration-doc], [canary-checklist].

Recap (short): staged Dedicated pilot recommended, run targeted quantized evals before expanding, finance to review blended economics, action items assigned with due dates.
